title: A name on the Helm hub
notes: One name on the hub: an output such as the Twister, or a responsibility
such as itajara:switches. The hub keeps one of these machines per name.
Who holds the name is NOT a state. The hub behaves the same whoever the
holder is, so the holder's identity stays in the host, and reaches the
machine as one fact about each request: was it sent by the holder. That
is the elevator's lesson about floors, applied to connections.
A grant therefore stays in 'held': the holder changes and the mode does
not. The frames the hub sends in reply (claims, wanted, refused, asked)
are not in this machine either. Glassbox commands belong to entering and
leaving a state, and most of the hub's replies happen on a request that
changes no state. They are pinned by the scenarios in helm-hub.json.
What this machine does pin: which requests change whether the name is
held, which are refused, and why.
Written 2026-11-13 from hub/hub.mjs as it stood, as part of the wire
declarations spike. hub/conformance-machine.mjs drives the real hub
through every vector generated from this file.
